reuse.why: getNextDate gets a small firstWeekdayOccurrence helper, but getUpcomingDates in schedules/app.ts writes its own skip loop instead of sharing it, and the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend entry point is not extended to own the daily rule.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend => drop weekend occurrences' rule is implemented twice (firstWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts and an inline bounded loop in server/schedules/app.ts) with different bounds, and the daily condition is recomputed in each.

placement.why: The shared/schedules.ts part sits where the tree keeps date rules, but the server app grows its own copy of the rule rather than delegating to shared code.

scope.why: Changes are limited to the weekend rule, the frequency passthrough, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: The rule now lives in two divergent implementations and the third consumer (budget schedule-template, which re-applies getDateWithSkippedWeekend after getNextDate with noSkipWeekend) still moves daily weekend dates, so future changes must be made in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates implements its own weekend-skip loop instead of using the shared helper; server/budget/schedule-template.ts keeps calling getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly for daily schedules

disguised_duplication.where: getUpcomingDates' for-loop with take count*7+7 and isWeekend filter is a reshaped copy of firstWeekdayOccurrence (find over take 7) in shared/schedules.ts

one_place.where: Rule implemented separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still applies the old move rule to daily schedules
